title: Wash, condition, stretch and detangle before braiding
course_title: Hair Care & Simple Styling: Salon Service Practice

say: Wash, condition, stretch and detangle before braiding.
This is the video for module 2 of Hair Care and Simple Styling.
Neat, long-lasting braids start before the first part. The hair must be clean, conditioned, and detangled without breaking strands.

panel.heading: Neat braids start with good prep
items: Clean, conditioned hair
Detangled without breaking strands
Stretched, so parts are clean
Fully dry before extensions go in

say: It must also be stretched, because coily hair shrinks as it dries, and fully dry before extensions go in. Damp hair sealed inside braids dries very slowly.

say: Many home salons have no basin. Two buckets are enough.
Bucket A holds lukewarm water. Mix hot into cold, never the other way round, and test it on the inside of your wrist.

say: Coily hair tangles when it is scrubbed in one big mass. So first divide the dry hair into 4 to 6 sections and twist each one.

panel.heading: The sectioned wash
items: Divide dry hair into 4 to 6 twisted sections
Wet one section with the jug
Shampoo the scalp only, with finger pads
Rinse until clear, then condition the length
Wrap in a towel to absorb water

say: Wet one section at a time, letting the water run into Bucket B.

say: Put a small amount of shampoo on the scalp only, and work it with the pads of your fingers, never your nails.

say: Rinse until the water runs clear and the hair no longer feels slippery. Leftover product can make the scalp itchy under braids. Then condition the length.

say: For example, Bisi runs a home salon in Ibadan and wants to know what a wash costs her.
A 500 ml bottle of shampoo costs about 4,500 naira. One wash uses about 20 ml, so that is 180 naira.
Conditioner at about 5,000 naira for 500 ml, using 30 ml, is 300 naira.
Two jerrycans of water at about 100 naira each is 200 naira.
That is about 680 naira in materials, before her time. Prices are approximate, so measure your own usage with a marked cup.

You can stretch with heat. Blow-dry damp, not dripping, hair on the lowest heat that works, with a heat protectant, moving the dryer from root to ends. If the hair smells burnt or the ends feel crispy, the heat is too high.
Or use African threading: wrap soft thread down each section and leave it to dry overnight. It is gentle on fine hair. If she feels tightness at the root, unwind and wrap more loosely.
Detangling is where most salon damage happens. Work on damp hair with a conditioner or detangler that gives slip, and a wide-tooth comb.

panel.heading: Detangle from the ends up
items: Damp hair, with a product that gives slip
A section no wider than your palm
Fingers first, feeling for knots
Comb the ends, then move up slowly
Re-spray any section that dries

say: Take a section no wider than your palm and clip the rest away.

say: Separate it gently with your fingers first.

say: Hold the hair firmly a little above where you comb. Comb the last few centimetres first, then move up a little at a time until the comb glides from root to tip.

say: The commonest mistake is combing a section that has dried and shrunk. Keep the spray bottle at hand. And big sections hurt more and break more hair.

say: When braids come out, clients are often shocked by the loose hair. Explain calmly. Shed hair cannot fall out while braided, and shedding 50 to 100 hairs a day is normal. A shed hair has a small white bulb.

cards.d: Has a small white bulb at one end. Shedding 50 to 100 hairs a day is normal.
Short pieces with no bulb. Note it on her card, especially if it comes from the edges.
Remove shed hair and buildup with your fingers first, or water mats it into knots.

say: Short pieces with no bulb are breakage. Write that on her card, especially if it comes from the edges.

cards.d: Has a small white bulb at one end. Shedding 50 to 100 hairs a day is normal.
Short pieces with no bulb. Note it on her card, especially if it comes from the edges.
Remove shed hair and buildup with your fingers first, or water mats it into knots.

say: Remove the shed hair with your fingers before you wet it, or the water mats it into knots.

say: To remember. Test the water on your wrist. Wash in sections. Blot, never rub, and dry fully before braiding. Stretch with low heat or threading. Detangle damp hair in small sections, from the ends up.
With tender heads and children, take breaks and book more time instead of rushing.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Hot into cold, tested on your wrist
Section first; shampoo scalp, condition length
Blot, never rub; dry fully before braiding
Stretch with low heat or threading
Detangle damp, small sections, from the ends up
